title: The Jungle Prince, Chapter 3: A House in Yorkshire

sentences.en: So I kept hearing about this family from a long time back, and they were kind of semi-mythical figures themselves.
sentences.zh: 我一直听说这家人很久以前的事，他们自己也算是半神话式的人物了。

sentences.en: But I still don't know the true story of what happened to them.
sentences.zh: 但我至今仍不知道他们身上到底发生了什么真实的故事。

sentences.en: There was a lovely quote I read somewhere by the American Sanskrit scholar, Wendy Doniger.
sentences.zh: 我曾在某处读到过美国梵文学者温迪·多尼格尔的一句妙语。

sentences.en: Myths pick up the pieces where philosophy throws up its hands.
sentences.zh: 当哲学束手无策时，神话便接过了接力棒。

sentences.en: The great myths may help survivors to think through this unthinkable catastrophe, to make sense by analogy, drawing some sort of truth out of the chaos of life.
sentences.zh: 伟大的神话或许能帮助幸存者去思考这场不可思议的灾难，通过类比来理解现实，从生活的混沌中提炼出某种真理。

sentences.en: Chapter 3.
sentences.zh: 第三章。

sentences.en: A House in Yorkshire.
sentences.zh: 约克郡的一所房子。

sentences.en: A few days after I got back to London, I hopped on a train for Bradford in Yorkshire.
sentences.zh: 回到伦敦几天后，我搭上火车前往约克郡的布拉德福德。

sentences.en: It was farther north than I had ever been in England.
sentences.zh: 那是我在英国去过的最北边的地方。

sentences.en: When I got off the train, it was a blustery, rainy day.
sentences.zh: 下火车时，天气阴沉，风雨交加。

sentences.en: I walked from the bus stop past takeout Chinese, bedding parlors, vape shops, rows and rows of nearly identical brick houses.
sentences.zh: 我从公交车站走过，路过中餐外卖店、床上用品店、电子烟店，还有一排排几乎一模一样的砖房。

sentences.en: Their house is right next to a business hall.
sentences.zh: 他们的房子就在一个会堂隔壁。

sentences.en: Until I finally reached the address on the Western Union slips, the home of Shahid Bhatt, the man who identified himself as Cyrus's brother.
sentences.zh: 最终，我找到了西联汇款单上的地址，那是沙希德·巴特（Shahid Bhatt）的家，也就是那个自称是赛勒斯（Cyrus）兄弟的人的住处。

sentences.en: In front of me stood a neat small house with a trim patch of lawn.
sentences.zh: 出现在我面前的是一栋整洁的小房子，前面有一小块修剪整齐的草坪。

sentences.en: The yard was full of garden statues.
sentences.zh: 院子里摆满了花园雕像。

sentences.en: There must have been at least 40 of them.
sentences.zh: 至少有40个吧。

sentences.en: There were gnomes, fairies, Buddhas, leprechauns.
sentences.zh: 有地精、仙女、佛像，还有小妖精。

sentences.en: As I stood there, I realized how nervous I was.
sentences.zh: 站在那里时，我意识到自己有多紧张。

sentences.en: I paced in front of the house a little bit.
sentences.zh: 我在房子前踱来踱去。

sentences.en: It was just me and the gnomes.
sentences.zh: 只有我和那些雕像。

sentences.en: Hey look, it's Ellen Berry from the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 嘿，看，那是《纽约时报》的艾伦·贝里。

sentences.en: Hi Ellen.
sentences.zh: 你好，艾伦。

sentences.en: Good luck in there, Ellen.
sentences.zh: 祝你好运，艾伦。

sentences.en: And then I finally worked up the courage to ring the bell.
sentences.zh: 最后，我终于鼓起勇气按响了门铃。

sentences.en: And waited.
sentences.zh: 然后等待着。

sentences.en: The door was opened by a big man in one-piece tiger print pajamas.
sentences.zh: 门开了，一个穿着连体老虎纹睡衣的大块头男人站在门口。

sentences.en: He looked to be in his mid-80s.
sentences.zh: 他看起来有八十多岁了。

sentences.en: His eyes were cloudy with age.
sentences.zh: 他的双眼因年迈而浑浊。

sentences.en: But he was still imposing, barrel-chested, with hands that seemed twice the size of normal hands.
sentences.zh: 但他依然气势逼人，胸膛宽阔，那双手看起来比常人的大了一倍。

sentences.en: I could see that as a young man, he had been a giant.
sentences.zh: 我看得出，年轻时的他一定是个巨人。

sentences.en: But the thing that struck me most of all is that he had Cyrus's face.
sentences.zh: 但最让我震惊的是，他长着一张和赛勒斯一模一样的脸。

sentences.en: The same jutting cheekbones.
sentences.zh: 同样的颧骨突出。

sentences.en: The same pale skin.
sentences.zh: 同样的肤色苍白。

sentences.en: I introduced myself and told him why I was there.

sentences.en: I had known his brother.
sentences.zh: 我认识他的兄弟。

sentences.en: I wanted to understand the story of their family.
sentences.zh: 我想了解他们家族的故事。

sentences.en: A little to my surprise, he stepped back from the door and gestured for me to come in.
sentences.zh: 令我有些惊讶的是，他退后一步，示意我进去。

sentences.en: And I followed him into a small room at the front of the house.
sentences.zh: 我跟着他走进房子前部的一个小房间。

sentences.zh: 沙希德看起来越来越憔悴了。

sentences.zh: 她会坐在我身边，轻轻地催促他回忆与母亲在一起的早年时光。

sentences.en: My God.

sentences.zh: 她翻出了他们从德里收到的旧信件。

sentences.en: Letters from years ago, when Mickey still called himself Mickey.
sentences.zh: 那是多年前的信，那时米奇还叫自己米奇。

sentences.en: And they referred to their mother as Mommy.
sentences.zh: 他们称呼母亲为“妈咪”。

sentences.zh: 那是博德雷纳姆。

sentences.zh: 所以我正在去布拉德福德的路上。

sentences.en: I guess, um, Shahid is not well.
sentences.zh: 我想，嗯，沙希德不太好。

sentences.en: I, um, he had a fall, and he has a cheSt.
sentences.zh: 我，嗯，他摔了一跤，而且他胸部……

sentences.en: It was on my fourth visit to Bradford that something seemed to break loose for Shahid.
sentences.zh: 那是我第四次去布拉德福德，沙希德似乎终于敞开了心扉。

sentences.en: Shahid, which house burned down?
sentences.zh: 沙希德，哪栋房子烧毁了？

sentences.en: On that visit, he told me a story that was different from anything he had told me before.
sentences.zh: 在那次拜访中，他告诉我的故事与他之前说的截然不同。

sentences.en: It was a story about his family's experience of partition.
sentences.zh: 那是一个关于他家族经历印巴分治的故事。

sentences.en: The first to hold the office was Viscount Canning in 1858.
sentences.zh: 第一位担任该职位的是1858年的坎宁子爵。

sentences.en: This was right after World War II.
sentences.zh: 那是在二战结束后不久。

sentences.en: Great Britain had mobilized India's resources to fight that war, and in exchange, had promised the country full independence.
sentences.zh: 英国动员了印度的资源来打那场战争，作为交换，承诺给予印度完全独立。

sentences.en: So once the war ended, Britain had to make good on its promise.
sentences.zh: 所以战争一结束，英国就必须兑现承诺。

sentences.en: At Delhi, Lord Louis Mountbatten arrives to take up his appointment as India's viceroy
sentences.zh: 在德里，路易斯·蒙巴顿勋爵抵达，就任印度总督。

sentences.en: The government instructed its new viceroy, Lord Mountbatten, to deliver India's independence and get Britain out as quickly and smoothly as possible, to find the least worst way to
sentences.zh: 政府指示新任总督蒙巴顿勋爵，要实现印度的独立，并让英国尽可能快、尽可能平稳地撤离，找到最不坏的方式来……

sentences.en: retreat from India.
sentences.zh: 从印度撤军。

sentences.en: Religious violence was breaking out across the country, and Muslims were demanding a state of their own.
sentences.zh: 全国各地爆发了宗教暴力冲突，穆斯林要求建立属于自己的国家。

sentences.en: And so the British decided to create not one country, but two.
sentences.zh: 于是英国人决定不再建立一个国家，而是两个。

sentences.en: India would be majority Hindu.
sentences.zh: 印度将以印度教徒为主。

sentences.en: Pakistan would be majority Muslim.
sentences.zh: 巴基斯坦将以穆斯林为主。

sentences.en: Mountbatten had a year to divide things up.
sentences.zh: 蒙巴顿有一年的时间来划分这些事务。

sentences.en: But he also had a promotion in the Navy that he wanted to get back to.
sentences.zh: 但他还在海军有个职位等着他回去晋升。

sentences.en: He moved the deadline up by 10 months, and appointed another official, a legal scholar, who had never set foot in India, to carve up the territory instead.
sentences.zh: 他把最后期限提前了10个月，并任命了另一位从未踏足过印度的法律学者来负责划分领土。

sentences.en: He gave him five weeks to do it.
sentences.zh: 他只给了他五周时间来完成。

sentences.en: So he drew the lines, and set in motion one of the largest forced migrations in human history.
sentences.zh: 于是他划下了界线，并引发了人类历史上最大规模的强制移民之一。

sentences.en: For Shahid's family, prosperous, educated Muslims, it meant the end of life as they knew it.
sentences.zh: 对于沙希德那富有且受过教育的穆斯林家庭来说，这意味着他们所熟悉的生活彻底终结了。

sentences.en: Shahid's father had a plum job as the registrar of Lucknow University in India.
sentences.zh: 沙希德的父亲在印度勒克瑙大学担任教务长，那是一份肥差。

sentences.en: But he wanted to join the stream of Muslims headed for Karachi, Pakistan, where they would make up the government of a brand new country.
sentences.zh: 但他想加入前往巴基斯坦卡拉奇的穆斯林大军，他们将在那里建立一个全新国家的政府。

sentences.en: But his mother, Belayat, flatly refused to go.
sentences.zh: 但他的母亲贝利亚特断然拒绝离开。

sentences.en: All the relatives I spoke with remembered her as a fiery, forceful woman.
sentences.zh: 我采访过的所有亲戚都记得她是一位火爆、强势的女性。

sentences.en: Lucknow was her home.
sentences.zh: 勒克瑙是她的家。

sentences.en: She didn't want to give up her elegant house, which overlooked one of the palaces of the city's great hero, the Nawab of Avad.
sentences.zh: 她不想放弃她那座优雅的房子，那房子俯瞰着这座城市伟大英雄——阿瓦德纳瓦布的一座宫殿。

sentences.en: The family was deadlocked.
sentences.zh: 家族陷入了僵局。

sentences.en: And then, an event decided it for them.
sentences.zh: 然后，一件事情替他们做了决定。

sentences.en: Inayat Bhatt, Shahid's father, was riding his bicycle home one day, when he was stopped by a group of young Hindu men.
sentences.zh: 有一天，沙希德的父亲伊纳亚特·巴特正骑自行车回家，被一群年轻的印度教男子拦住了。

sentences.en: They began to whack him over the head with hockey sticks.
sentences.zh: 他们开始用曲棍球棒猛击他的头部。

sentences.en: Someone drew a knife.
sentences.zh: 有人拔出了刀。

sentences.en: And by the time he got home, this is what Shahid said, his hand was cut to the bone.
sentences.zh: 当他回到家时，沙希德说，他的手被砍到了骨头。

sentences.en: As he described it, I could almost see it.
sentences.zh: 当他描述这一幕时，我几乎能亲眼看到。

sentences.en: This distinguished man, his spectacles askew, knocked to the ground.
sentences.zh: 这位尊贵的绅士，眼镜歪斜，被击倒在地。

sentences.en: And so, a decision was made.
sentences.zh: 于是，决定做出了。

sentences.en: Shahid's family was going to Pakistan.
sentences.zh: 沙希德一家要搬去巴基斯坦。

sentences.en: They were among the 15 million who were uprooted from their homes by partition.
sentences.zh: 他们是因分治而被迫背井离乡的1500万人之一。

sentences.en: Muslims headed for Pakistan, and Hindus and Sikhs headed in the other direction.
sentences.zh: 穆斯林前往巴基斯坦，印度教徒和锡克教徒则朝另一个方向走去。

sentences.en: Trains of refugees going to and from Pakistan arrived loaded with corpses, the passengers slaughtered by mobs along the way.
sentences.zh: 往返于巴基斯坦的难民列车上装满了尸体，乘客在途中被暴徒屠杀。

sentences.en: Partition has become a byword for horror.
sentences.zh: “分治”已成为恐怖的代名词。

sentences.en: In his book about partition, Nisid Hajari described it this way.
sentences.zh: 尼西德·哈贾里在他关于分治的书里是这样描述的。

sentences.en: An appalling slaughter ensued.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是骇人听闻的屠杀。

sentences.en: Unending waves of refugees watched over the East Punjab.
sentences.zh: 无尽的难民潮涌向东旁遮普。

sentences.en: They left grim reminders of their passage.
sentences.zh: 他们留下了残酷的痕迹。

sentences.en: Gangs of killers set whole villages...
sentences.zh: 杀手团伙将整个村庄……

sentences.en: Trees stripped of bark, which they peeled off in great chunks to use as fuel.
sentences.zh: 树皮被剥光，他们剥下大块树皮用作燃料。

sentences.en: Dead and dying bullocks, cattle and sheep.
sentences.zh: 死去的和垂死的牛、羊。

sentences.en: And thousands and thousands of corpses lying alongside the road or buried shallowly.
sentences.zh: 成千上万具尸体躺在路边或被浅浅地掩埋。

sentences.en: Vultures feasted so extravagantly, they could no longer fly.
sentences.zh: 秃鹫吃得太饱，已经飞不起来了。

sentences.en: So-called corpse trains rolled into Lahore station, dripping blood.
sentences.zh: 所谓的“尸体列车”开进拉合尔车站，滴着血。

sentences.en: And a carriages filled and hacked off limbs.
sentences.zh: 车厢里塞满了被砍下的肢体。

sentences.en: And women without breasts or noses.
sentences.zh: 还有被割掉乳房或鼻子的妇女。

sentences.en: And babies hacked out of 14 million refugees.
sentences.zh: 还有从1400万难民中被剖出来的婴儿。

sentences.en: Infants were found literally.
sentences.zh: 婴儿被发现时简直……

sentences.en: The conflagration stands as one of the deadliest and most brutal civil conflicts of the 20th century.
sentences.zh: 这场大火灾是20世纪最致命、最残酷的内战冲突之一。

sentences.en: There are no good estimates of how many people died.
sentences.zh: 没有人能准确估计到底死了多少人。

sentences.en: But Shahid and his family made it through.
sentences.zh: 但沙希德和他的家人挺过来了。

sentences.en: They set up a new household in Karachi.
sentences.zh: 他们在卡拉奇安了新家。

sentences.en: His older brothers joined the Pakistani Air Force.
sentences.zh: 他的哥哥们加入了巴基斯坦空军。

sentences.en: And his father, according to relatives, got a new job in the Civil Aviation Authority.
sentences.zh: 据亲戚说，他的父亲在民航局找到了一份新工作。

sentences.en: But there was still no peace in the house.
sentences.zh: 但家里依然不得安宁。

sentences.en: Shahid said his mother was angry.
sentences.zh: 沙希德说他的母亲很愤怒。

sentences.en: She was angry about what had been taken from her.
sentences.zh: 她对被夺走的一切感到愤怒。

sentences.en: What she was forced to leave behind in India.
sentences.zh: 对她被迫留在印度的一切感到愤怒。

sentences.en: She wouldn't accept it.
sentences.zh: 她无法接受这一切。

sentences.en: She lobbied Pakistani officials for her lost properties.
sentences.zh: 她游说巴基斯坦官员，试图要回她失去的财产。

sentences.en: And then one day, Shahid said, she crossed a line.
sentences.zh: 然后有一天，沙希德说，她越界了。

sentences.en: I've heard versions of this story from almost everyone I've contacted.
sentences.zh: 我从联系过的几乎每个人那里都听过这个故事的版本。

sentences.en: And I'm piecing it together.
sentences.zh: 我正在把它们拼凑起来。

sentences.en: There was a scene in a public place.
sentences.zh: 那是在一个公共场合发生的场景。

sentences.en: Valet confronted a government official, maybe even the prime minister, at a public event and demanded the return of her property.
sentences.zh: 贝利亚特在一次公开活动中与一位政府官员，甚至可能是总理对质，要求归还她的财产。

sentences.en: Whatever the official said in response, it didn't go well.
sentences.zh: 无论那位官员说了什么，结果都不太好。

sentences.en: She slapped him.
sentences.zh: 她扇了他一巴掌。

sentences.en: And then this proud, defiant woman was arrested, confined for six months to a mental hospital.
sentences.zh: 然后这位骄傲、倔强的女人被捕了，被关进精神病院六个月。

sentences.en: And, one relative told me, was treated with electroshock therapy.
sentences.zh: 而且，一位亲戚告诉我，她还接受了电击疗法。

sentences.en: Shahid was still young when this happened.
sentences.zh: 发生这件事时，沙希德还很小。

sentences.en: What was the hospital like?
sentences.zh: 那家医院是什么样的？

sentences.en: What was the hospital like?
sentences.zh: 那家医院是什么样的？

sentences.en: Tell me.
sentences.zh: 告诉我。

sentences.en: Medivh.
sentences.zh: 梅迪夫。

sentences.en: On my last visit with him, as Camelia and I sat by his bed,
sentences.zh: 在我最后一次探望他时，我和卡米莉亚坐在他的床边，

sentences.en: he remembered visiting his mother in what was then known as the Punjab Mental Asylum.
sentences.zh: 他回忆起去探望他母亲的情景，当时那里被称为旁遮普精神病院。

sentences.en: He recalled one girl who had been bound to the wall with four chains, two on her hands, two on her feet,
sentences.zh: 他记得有个女孩被四条铁链锁在墙上，双手各一条，双脚各一条，

sentences.en: spitting furiously at anyone who walked by.
sentences.zh: 对着路过的每一个人愤怒地吐口水。

sentences.en: She got electroshock therapy.
sentences.zh: 她接受了电击疗法。

sentences.en: His mother was no longer fiery.
sentences.zh: 他的母亲不再火爆了。

sentences.en: She did not proteSt.
sentences.zh: 她没有抗议。

sentences.en: And what was her state?
sentences.zh: 那她的状态如何？

sentences.en: Was she still as fiery?
sentences.zh: 她还像以前那样火爆吗？

sentences.en: Or was she quiet, subdued?
sentences.zh: 还是说她当时很安静，情绪低落？

sentences.en: Quiet.
sentences.zh: 很安静。

sentences.en: Shahid said she just sat in a chair, quiet.
sentences.zh: 沙希德说她只是坐在椅子上，很安静。

sentences.en: Did they put her there to teach her a lesson?
sentences.zh: 他们把她放在那儿是为了给她点教训吗？

sentences.en: God, no.
sentences.zh: 天哪，不是。

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我觉得是。

sentences.en: I think it was to quieten her.
sentences.zh: 我觉得是为了让她安静下来。

sentences.en: One small girl was sitting up to a wall.
sentences.zh: 一个小女孩正靠着墙坐着。

sentences.en: Oh, God.
sentences.zh: 噢，天哪。

sentences.en: It was clear from the look on his face that all these years later, he had not quite recovered.
sentences.zh: 从他脸上的表情可以清楚地看出，多年以后，他仍未完全走出来。

sentences.en: Hello.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: I'm not well.
sentences.zh: 我不太舒服。

sentences.en: He never told you about the mental hospital?
sentences.zh: 他从没跟你提过那家精神病院吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Never spoke about it to me before.
sentences.zh: 以前从没跟我提起过。

sentences.en: Who was it?
sentences.zh: 那是谁？

sentences.en: No, she was.
sentences.zh: 不，是她。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 噢，不。

sentences.en: It was sometime after she was released from the institution,
sentences.zh: 那是在她出院后不久，

sentences.en: Shahid couldn't say exactly when, that she decided to return to India.
sentences.zh: 沙希德说不清具体是什么时候，她决定回印度。

sentences.en: She told relatives she was going back to retrieve her property.
sentences.zh: 她告诉亲戚她要回去拿回属于她的财产。

sentences.en: Some of them had the sense that she was going to pursue a career in politics.
sentences.zh: 他们中有些人觉得她是想去从政。

sentences.en: She packed her household belongings in trunks and gathered together her youngest children.
sentences.zh: 她把家当装进箱子，带上了她最小的几个孩子。

sentences.en: Family said she smuggled them across the border illegally.
sentences.zh: 家人说她是偷渡带他们过境的。

sentences.en: Shahid was one of the children she took, the oldeSt.
sentences.zh: 沙希德是她带走的孩子之一，也是最大的那个。

sentences.en: But somewhere along that journey, Shahid said it was in Bombay.
sentences.zh: 但在那段旅程中的某个地方，沙希德说是孟买。

sentences.en: He decided he couldn't go along with his mother anymore.
sentences.zh: 他决定不再跟随母亲了。

sentences.en: At one point, Vilayat asked him to go out and buy bananas.
sentences.zh: 有一次，维拉亚特让他出去买香蕉。

sentences.en: She gave him some money, and he took the money in his hand,
sentences.zh: 她给了他一些钱，他接过钱，

sentences.en: walked out onto the street, and never came back.
sentences.zh: 走到街上，就再也没回来。

sentences.en: He didn't give them any explanation.
sentences.zh: 他没有给他们任何解释。

sentences.en: And he never saw his mother again.
sentences.zh: 从此他再也没见过他母亲。

sentences.en: And it's sometime after that, that Vilayat Bhatt and her two youngest children,
sentences.zh: 那之后不久，维拉亚特·巴特和她最小的两个孩子，

sentences.en: Mickey and Farhad Bhatt, appeared at the railway station and set up a home in the VIP waiting room.
sentences.zh: 米奇和法哈德·巴特，出现在火车站，并在贵宾候车室安了家。

sentences.en: She was no longer the wife of a university registrar.
sentences.zh: 她不再是大学注册官的妻子了。

sentences.en: Her children were no longer citizens of Pakistan.
sentences.zh: 她的孩子们也不再是巴基斯坦公民了。

sentences.en: They had new names,
sentences.zh: 他们有了新的名字，

sentences.en: new titles, and a single, impossible mission.
sentences.zh: 新的头衔，以及一个不可能完成的任务。

sentences.en: They were now the royal family of Avad.
sentences.zh: 他们现在是阿瓦德的皇室家族。

sentences.en: I guess what I wonder is, do you think that it was partition that ruined your mother's life?
sentences.zh: 我想知道的是，你认为是因为印巴分治毁了你母亲的一生吗？

sentences.en: Yes?
sentences.zh: 是吗？

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Well, we had to start all over again.

sentences.zh: 沙希德没再多说什么。

sentences.en: His storehouse of memories seemed to shut just as quickly as it had opened.
sentences.zh: 他的记忆仓库似乎刚打开就又关上了。

sentences.en: He wouldn't watch Petition, you know, last year.
sentences.zh: 你知道，去年他都不肯看关于分治的节目。

sentences.en: Oh, really?
sentences.zh: 噢，真的吗？

sentences.en: I had every program on that was on about it.
sentences.zh: 当时所有相关的节目我都看了。

sentences.en: And I said, Shahid, come and look at it.
sentences.zh: 我说，沙希德，过来看看。

sentences.en: No, no, I don't want to.
sentences.zh: 不，不，我不想看。

sentences.en: No, I was there.
sentences.zh: 不，我当时就在那儿。

sentences.en: I don't want to see it on TV.
sentences.zh: 我不想在电视上看到它。

sentences.en: He just did not want to see it.
sentences.zh: 他就是不想看。

sentences.en: It's not like Germany, where there's been lots and lots of processing of, you know, this is what the deaths were, and who killed them, and who's responsible,
sentences.zh: 这不像德国，那里对历史进行了大量的处理，你知道，比如死亡人数是多少，谁杀了他们，谁该负责，

sentences.en: and how we can deal with the history.
sentences.zh: 以及我们该如何面对这段历史。

sentences.en: It's almost like it all just got papered over.
sentences.zh: 这儿几乎就像是被掩盖了一样。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: In some ways, you could understand Valiat's anger.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，你可以理解维拉亚特的愤怒。

sentences.en: I find it very, very sad.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这非常、非常悲哀。

sentences.en: But it also consumed her children.
sentences.zh: 但这同时也吞噬了她的孩子们。

sentences.en: I think what started off as a ruse
sentences.zh: 我想最初只是一个计谋，

sentences.en: became too big for them.
sentences.zh: 后来对他们来说变得太大了。

sentences.en: Or became the reality for them?
sentences.zh: 还是说那成了他们的现实？

sentences.en: Or just was a ruse that they had to continue until the end?
sentences.zh: 或者只是一个他们必须坚持到底的计谋？

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: And then it became a way of life.
sentences.zh: 然后它就变成了一种生活方式。

sentences.en: Well, I suppose once you've sacrificed 20 years of your life to an idea, to admit that it was all...
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想一旦你为一个理念牺牲了20年的生命，要承认这一切都……

sentences.en: It can become part of your life then, and you can half believe it.
sentences.zh: 那它就能成为你生命的一部分，你甚至会半信半疑。

sentences.en: Do you live the life that long that you have to believe it, or what?
sentences.zh: 你是活得太久以至于不得不相信它，还是怎么回事？

sentences.en: He does all of the unclaimed bodies.
sentences.zh: 他负责处理所有无人认领的尸体。

sentences.en: After Cyrus died, I tried to find out where he was buried.
sentences.zh: 赛勒斯死后，我试图查明他被埋在哪里。

sentences.en: The police who came to collect his body at the hunting lodge couldn't identify any next of kin, or any friend, or even any acquaintance.
sentences.zh: 在狩猎小屋收走他尸体的警察无法确认任何亲属、朋友，甚至熟人。

sentences.en: So they assigned his body a number, DD33B, and sent it to a pauper's graveyard on the edge of Old Delhi, an expanse of uneven, scrubby land beside a cricket stadium.
sentences.zh: 于是他们给他的尸体编了个号，DD33B，并把它送到了旧德里边缘的一个贫民墓地，那是一片位于板球场旁、土地凹凸不平且长满灌木的地方。

sentences.en: When an unclaimed body, like Cyrus's, comes in, they bury them wherever there's an empty space, between other graves.
sentences.zh: 当像赛勒斯这样无人认领的尸体送来时，他们就把他们埋在任何有空位的地方，在其他坟墓之间。

sentences.en: The land is porous, so the bodies sink, and they bury other bodies over them.
sentences.zh: 土地是疏松的，所以尸体会下沉，他们又会在上面埋葬其他尸体。

sentences.en: They mark these graves with a shard of pink rock, and that's all.
sentences.zh: 他们只用一块粉红色的岩石碎片来标记这些坟墓，仅此而已。

sentences.en: So there was no way to know where Cyrus was.
sentences.zh: 所以根本无法知道赛勒斯在哪里。

sentences.en: I wandered around for some time, from one mound to another,
sentences.zh: 我在那儿徘徊了一会儿，从一个土堆走到另一个土堆，

sentences.en: and then sat down next to a tree.
sentences.zh: 然后在一棵树旁坐了下来。

sentences.en: I took out my notebook and wrote,
sentences.zh: 我拿出笔记本写道：

sentences.en: He's lost in a city of the dead.
sentences.zh: 他迷失在死者之城里。

sentences.en: The story I had to tell about him was grim as well.
sentences.zh: 关于他的故事也同样凄凉。

sentences.en: Not of a returning warrior queen, but of two children who followed their mother into the woods and never came out.
sentences.zh: 不是关于一位回归的战士女王，而是关于两个跟随母亲走进森林却再也没出来的孩子。

sentences.en: Cyrus would have hated that story.
sentences.zh: 赛勒斯会讨厌那个故事的。

sentences.en: I was unraveling the central work of his family's life.
sentences.zh: 我正在拆解他家族生命中的核心工作。

sentences.en: I walked back to the entrance of the cemetery and asked the clerk to look through his records of unclaimed bodies one more time,
sentences.zh: 我走回墓地入口，请职员再查一遍无人认领尸体的记录，

sentences.en: on the off chance that I could find him.
sentences.zh: 希望能碰碰运气找到他。

sentences.en: And at least mark his grave.
sentences.zh: 至少能标记一下他的坟墓。

sentences.en: And that's when I noticed a man sitting in the room, listening to us intently.
sentences.zh: 就在那时，我注意到房间里坐着一个人，正全神贯注地听着我们说话。

sentences.en: He was wearing a voluminous, cheap-looking tweed jacket, and he had a squiff of jet-black dyed hair bobbing over his forehead.
sentences.zh: 他穿着一件宽大、看起来很廉价的粗花呢夹克，额头上有一撮染成漆黑的头发在晃动。

sentences.en: He stood up and introduced himself, rather formally.
sentences.zh: 他站起来，相当正式地做了自我介绍。

sentences.en: He handed me a plastic folder.
sentences.zh: 他递给我一个塑料文件夹。

sentences.en: It was filled with newspaper clippings about Cyrus' death.
sentences.zh: 里面装满了关于赛勒斯死讯的剪报。

sentences.en: He told me that he carries the clippings around with him every day.
sentences.zh: 他告诉我，他每天都随身带着这些剪报。

sentences.en: In Old Delhi, he told me.
sentences.zh: 在旧德里，他告诉我。

sentences.en: This was the only topic of conversation from street to street and from house to house.
sentences.zh: 这是街头巷尾唯一的话题。

sentences.en: People were saying, such a big king passed away like this in such a way that nobody knew him.
sentences.zh: 人们都在说，这么伟大的国王竟然以这种方式去世，以至于没人认识他。

sentences.en: How can the scion of such an illustrious royal family get lost in the darkness of oblivion?
sentences.zh: 这样一个显赫皇室家族的后裔，怎么会迷失在遗忘的黑暗中呢？

sentences.en: The man had become visibly distraught and began to recite verses of Urdu poetry, asking God why he had done such a thing, brought low the rulers of Avad,
sentences.zh: 那人显然变得心烦意乱，开始背诵乌尔都语诗句，质问上帝为什么要这样做，让阿瓦德的统治者沦落至此，

sentences.en: because they all knew the story.
sentences.zh: 因为他们都知道这个故事。

sentences.en: Fifty years ago, a woman appeared on a train platform.
sentences.zh: 五十年前，一个女人出现在火车站台上。

sentences.en: She had been dispossessed.
sentences.zh: 她被剥夺了一切。

sentences.en: Her family had been torn in half.
sentences.zh: 她的家庭被撕裂了。

sentences.en: She had come to reclaim what had been taken from her.
sentences.zh: 她回来是为了夺回被夺走的东西。

sentences.en: The people who came to see her, they were also dispossessed.
sentences.zh: 那些来看她的人，也同样被剥夺了一切。

sentences.en: Their families had also been torn in half.
sentences.zh: 他们的家庭也同样被撕裂了。

sentences.en: And this man in front of me had revered the royal family for so long.
sentences.zh: 而我面前的这个人，长期以来一直崇敬着这个皇室家族。

sentences.en: The story had sounded a note within him.
sentences.zh: 这个故事在他心中引起了共鸣。

sentences.en: He would be telling it for years.
sentences.zh: 他会讲述这个故事很多年。

sentences.en: It would be passed among tea sellers and auto rickshaw drivers.
sentences.zh: 它会在茶摊老板和自动人力车司机之间流传。

sentences.en: The story about the prince who lived in a palace, in the jungle, in the middle of the city.
sentences.zh: 关于那个住在城市中心丛林里宫殿中的王子的故事。

sentences.en: And they'll be telling that story long after my story has come and gone.
sentences.zh: 即使我的故事早已被人遗忘，他们依然会讲述那个故事。

sentences.en: I will be, I cannot forget you.
sentences.zh: 我会的，我无法忘记你。

sentences.en: Most welcome whenever you feel like you are dead.
sentences.zh: 随时欢迎你，只要你觉得你已经死了。

sentences.en: So it's all about you.
sentences.zh: 所以这都是关于你的事。

sentences.en: Well, I'm not leaving yet.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我还没打算离开。

sentences.en: I'm just thinking about the future.
sentences.zh: 我只是在考虑未来。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: Of course, future.
sentences.zh: 当然，未来。

sentences.en: But one more thing.
sentences.zh: 但还有一件事。

sentences.en: I really want that it should crumble.
sentences.zh: 我真的希望它能崩塌。

sentences.en: If it hasn't crumbled for the last 600 years, it's not going to crumble this week.
sentences.zh: 如果它在过去600年里都没崩塌，那这周也不会崩塌。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: Very true.
sentences.zh: 说得太对了。

sentences.en: Very true.
sentences.zh: 说得太对了。

sentences.zh: 说得太对了。

sentences.zh: 你给自己找了一座非常稳固的城堡。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I have a roof, a very strong roof.
sentences.zh: 我有一个屋顶，一个非常坚固的屋顶。

sentences.en: That's all.
sentences.zh: 仅此而已。

sentences.en: And pillar to hide and pillar to protect myself.
sentences.zh: 还有可以躲藏和保护自己的支柱。

sentences.en: That's all.
sentences.zh: 仅此而已。

sentences.en: Well, it's something to be proud of.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这值得骄傲。

sentences.en: Not everyone lives in a place like this.
sentences.zh: 不是每个人都住在这样的地方。

sentences.en: You see a little light over there in that ark.
sentences.zh: 你看到那个拱门里有一点光吗？

sentences.en: Just turn.
sentences.zh: 转过去。

sentences.en: I do.
sentences.zh: 我看到了。

sentences.zh: 那是从哪儿来的？

sentences.zh: 那只是倒影吗？

sentences.zh: 那是主要的烛光。

sentences.en: Wait, wait, wait.
sentences.zh: 等等，等等，等等。

sentences.zh: 我想看看它是不是还在一直亮着。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊，是啊。

sentences.zh: 你多久点一次蜡烛？

sentences.en: Candles?
sentences.zh: 蜡烛？

sentences.zh: 噢，你过来看看。

sentences.zh: 我能做些什么。

sentences.zh: 那边有一根很粗的柱子。

sentences.en: So I do place over there.
sentences.zh: 所以我把它放在那边。

sentences.en: That's a natural one.
sentences.zh: 那是天然的。

sentences.zh: 所以我喜欢这个，我们不希望任何人模仿我们。

sentences.en: Very romantic.
sentences.zh: 非常浪漫。

sentences.zh: 你可以带我去印出来。

sentences.en: Yes, I know.
sentences.zh: 是的，我知道。

sentences.en: I think it's too dark.
sentences.zh: 我觉得太暗了。

sentences.en: But anyway, make it up from your blind and watch.
sentences.zh: 但不管怎样，从你的百叶窗和手表上补救一下吧。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Wirecutter秀》，我们要为假期接待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人宾至如归的小贴士。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要全黑环境才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是不是喝到断片才睡着。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是说，他们需要什么样的光线环境？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为那是非常具体的要求。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？
